questions.explanation: 'Whereby' means 'by which', introducing the means or method.
questions.q: They devised a system ___ funds could be traced.

questions.explanation: 'Whereupon' means 'at which point', marking immediate sequence.
questions.q: The verdict was read, ___ the court erupted.
Choose the correct sentence.
options: The clause whereby the penalty is defined is notoriously vague.
The clause wherein the penalty is defined is notoriously vague.
The clause whereupon the penalty is defined is notoriously vague.
The clause whereof the penalty is defined is notoriously vague.
questions.explanation: 'Wherein' means 'in which', locating something within a document.
'Whereof' means 'of which', used in formal legal style.
questions.q: The will, the terms ___ are sealed, will be read tomorrow.
Which sentence is correct?
options: He returned to the village whence he had fled decades earlier.
He returned to the village whereby he had fled decades earlier.
He returned to the village whereupon he had fled decades earlier.
He returned to the village wherein he had fled decades earlier.
questions.explanation: 'Whence' means 'from where', used in formal or literary style.
'Whosoever' is the formal indefinite relative meaning 'whoever'.
questions.q: ___ breaks this seal shall answer to the court.

questions.explanation: 'Whereat' means 'at which', a formal relative of place or point.
questions.q: They reached an impasse, ___ negotiations collapsed.

questions.explanation: 'In which' is the standard relative; 'whereby' would wrongly mean 'by which'.
questions.q: The house ___ she grew up has been demolished.

questions.explanation: 'For which' is the correct preposition + relative for purpose.
questions.q: The grant, ___ the research was funded, came from the trust.

questions.explanation: 'Whom' is the object relative for people; 'which' cannot refer to a person.
questions.q: The envoy, ___ the king trusted, carried the message.
Identify the correct sentence.
options: The author, whereof novel won the prize, declined to comment.
The author, which novel won the prize, declined to comment.
The author, whose novel won the prize, declined to comment.
The author, whereby novel won the prize, declined to comment.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative; 'whereof' cannot show personal possession here.
'The which' is archaic; modern formal style uses 'which' alone.
questions.q: He cited the statute, ___ had been repealed.

questions.explanation: Only the 'whereupon' version correctly marks the immediate consequence.
options: The bell rang, whereupon the debate ended
The bell rang, whereby the debate ended
The bell rang, wherein the debate ended
The bell rang, whereof the debate ended
questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

questions.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative; 'whereof' cannot show personal possession here.
questions.q: The author, ___ novel won the prize, declined to comment.

questions.explanation: 'Wherein' = 'in which', fitting a provision contained within the agreement.
questions.q: The article ___ this right is enshrined was later amended.

questions.explanation: 'As' can introduce a relative clause referring to a whole preceding statement.
questions.q: He resigned, ___ surprised nobody.

questions.explanation: 'Whereby' expresses the means; the other relatives express place or time.
questions.q: Choose the relative meaning 'by means of which'.
Choose the correct version.
options: The truce was signed, whereby the guns fell silent.
The truce was signed, whereupon the guns fell silent.
The truce was signed, wherein the guns fell silent.
The truce was signed, whereof the guns fell silent.
